Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:43: The matter is further explained in the Tikkunim (beginning of 61), in these words: therefore the set time (onah) of Torah scholars is on Shabbat, for on the weekdays, when Metatron rules, "it shall be shut the six working days" (Ezekiel 46:1) — in this the gate is closed; but on the day of Shabbat the gate opens, and the Shechinah goes forth from it to unite with her husband — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:44: And in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot 78a) it explains the verse, "the nakedness of your daughter-in-law you shall not uncover" (Leviticus 18:15), regarding a Torah scholar on the weekdays not approaching his "daughter-in-law," who is his wife, in these words: "daughter-in-law" (kallah) in the supernal mystery is to show that whoever causes a blemish below causes a blemish above, for we have learned that the set time of Torah scholars is from Shabbat to Shabbat, because they know the mystery of the matter and direct their hearts, and their will is found complete; and because they beget [in this manner], they are called "children of the King." And if these cause a blemish in the matter below, it is as though they blemish the "bride" above; then it is written, "the nakedness of your daughter-in-law you shall not uncover" — for they know the ways of Torah. The rest of the people, for whom this literally means their daughter-in-law — through this sin the Shechinah withdraws from them — so far his words. This clearly shows the obligation upon a Torah scholar to separate from his wife on the weekdays, because they have union with the Shechinah through occupying themselves with Torah, whereas the rest of the people, who do not aspire to rise to the level of Torah and to become Torah scholars and unite with the Shechinah, cause the Shechinah to withdraw from them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:45: Further, it is elaborated in the Zohar (Parashat Yitro 89b) regarding the greatness of the set time of Torah scholars from Shabbat to Shabbat, on the verse, "unto the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths" (Isaiah 56:4), and regarding the punishment of the common people (amei ha'aretz) who do not conduct themselves so, calling the children of the common people "children of harlotry," because they do not practice the proper holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:46: Therefore every person is obligated to increase his Torah study and service every day until he becomes a Torah scholar, and merits to unite with the Shechinah and be among her servants who draw near to her, sanctified with her holiness. Therefore our holy Torah, in Parashat Kedoshim, at the beginning of its explanation of the matters of holiness, says, "Every man shall revere his mother and his father, and keep My Sabbaths" (Leviticus 19:3). Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains, in his interpretation of the verse (Parashat Kedoshim 82a), that these are the Torah scholars who abstain [from relations] all six weekdays to occupy themselves with Torah, and that the term "keep" (tishmoru) is like "and his father kept the matter (in mind)" (Genesis 37:11).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:47: Reason dictates that whoever does not rise [at midnight] has no yearning at all for the love of the Shechinah — for the beloved who follows his beloved does not slumber or sleep, out of the greatness of his love for her; and since this Torah scholar does not rise, the Shechinah complains against him that he has no love for her, since he neglects her set time and does not care for her, and the Holy One, blessed be He, likewise complains against him, for he neglects the set time of His daughter, who is the Torah — and Torah has already been likened to a king's beautiful, beloved daughter — see in the Zohar. As it is said, "Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance (morashah)" (Deuteronomy 33:4), and so on; and they said, of blessed memory, in Pesachim (49b): Rabbi Chiya taught, whoever studies Torah in front of an am ha'aretz (ignorant person) is as though he had relations with his betrothed in front of him, as it is said, "Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance (morashah)" — do not read "morashah" but "me'orasah" (betrothed).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:48: Concerning this it is said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi 207a) that David used to sleep only sixty "breaths," so that when midnight came he would rise and the Shechinah would not find him asleep, which is bound to the Other Side, in these words: and therefore King David used to measure the measure of the night, so that he would remain in life, and the taste of death would not rule over him; and when the night was divided, David remained steadfast in his place, because when midnight is aroused and the holy crown is aroused, he did not want to be found bound to another place, a place of death — for when midnight is divided and supernal holiness is aroused, and a person is asleep in his bed and does not awaken to consider the glory of his Master, behold he becomes bound in the mystery of death and attached to another place. Therefore King David always stood to consider the glory of his Master, life facing life, and did not sleep in slumber to the taste of death, and therefore he would doze like a horse for sixty breaths, and not fully — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:49: This shows that at midnight the supernal holiness is aroused, and the Shechinah is aroused and sends the souls below so that they may be aroused for the honor of their Maker; and whoever is aroused but does not rise does not consider the honor of his Maker. And the honor of the Shechinah is that a person be aroused through Torah, which is the Tree of Life, and through this she unites through the [mystery of] eighteen (chai) worlds — this is [the meaning of] "life facing life" — in the manner explained in the Zohar (Parashat Emor 90a), "the righteous shall inherit the land" (Psalms 37:29): that the Shechinah at midnight is between two righteous ones, the supernal Righteous One and the lower righteous one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:50: And in the Zohar (Parashat Bamidbar 119a) it says that the Holy One, blessed be He, returns the souls to Israel at midnight so that they may occupy themselves with Torah, in these words: and should you say, there are indeed many people who awaken at night while the tree of death still rules, [and] that tree of death is what causes it? Why is this? Because it is written, "to see if there be any that acts wisely, that seeks after God" (Psalms 14:2), and a person should have no excuse to say, "had I ruled over my soul, I would have occupied myself at night with Torah" — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:51: This shows that the return of the soul at midnight applies both to the common person and to the Torah scholar; and if it were not incumbent upon the common person to rise and occupy himself with Torah, why would the Holy One, blessed be He, return his soul? Rather, certainly, so that a person takes this to heart and says, "Not for nothing did the Holy One, blessed be He, return my soul to me at this hour, but so that I occupy myself with Torah." And he should add to this every single day, as they said (Avot 1:13), "and whoever does not add, loses" — the reason being that if he does not add, he dries up, and is found like a tree that bears no fruit and has no use except to be burned. And so the statement of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (87a), in these words: woe to those people who do not occupy themselves with Torah, who are called dry trees, destined to be burned in the fire of Gehinnom; and not for nothing did the masters of the Mishnah establish that they toil and inherit Gehinnom — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:52: Further, regarding the punishment of one who does not rise, and the reward if he does rise, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra 23a), in these words: Rabbi Yosei opened and said, "but none says, Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night" (Job 35:10). Come and see, at the hour the north wind is aroused and the night is divided, we have established that a single flame goes out and strikes beneath the wings of the rooster, and it strikes its wings and crows, and that flame, at the time it reaches and is aroused against it, looks at it and trembles, and crows, and is silent, and gazes because of the honor of its Master, to do His will, and calls out to the people. Therefore it is called "sechvi" (rooster, related to "gazing") — it gazes — and is called "gever" (mighty one), because it awakens through the flame of Gevurah, coming from the side of Gevurah to awaken in the world; then those people of faith stand and give strength to the Community of Israel, and this is called "the song of Torah"; and therefore David inherited the kingship, he and his sons forever, for all generations. And when the rooster crows and people are asleep in their beds and do not awaken, the rooster crows again and says what it says — as has been established — toward morning it strikes its wings [again] — woe to so-and-so, rebuked by his Master, forsaken by his Master, that he does not awaken his spirit and does not consider the honor of his Master. When day dawns, a herald proclaims concerning him and says, "but none says, Where is God my Maker, who gives..." "in the night" — to assist him with those praises and to be all in one assistance. It should have said "osi" (my Maker) — why does it say "osai" [in the plural form, hinting at renewal]? Rather, at the hour a person rises at midnight and occupies himself with song — for the "song of Torah" is called such only at night — and when he is found engaged in Torah as day dawns, the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel prepare him and make him anew every day, to shine among those above and those below — so far his words, as pertains to us. And Rabbi Abba explains there regarding "osai" that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel prepare him and make him a new creature every single day, as it is said, "Let Israel rejoice in its Makers (osav)" (Psalms 149:2).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:53: From this passage it appears that the reward is great for one who rises at midnight to occupy himself with Torah, and likewise his punishment if he does not rise — for it says that the supernal herald calls him "rebuked by his Master... who does not awaken his spirit and does not consider the honor of his Master." And it says "does not awaken his spirit," because the soul comes to a person at midnight, as explained in the preceding passage from Parashat Bamidbar; but it is required that when the soul comes to him, his spirit be awakened to rise and give honor to his Creator by occupying himself with Torah, and that he not be lazy in such a way that he goes back to sleep, as it is said, "laziness casts into a deep sleep" (Proverbs 19:15). Rather, with alacrity he should rise to His service, blessed be He, for the awakening of the spirit indicates alacrity — like servants of a king who serve their master with alacrity to find favor in his eyes, and appear to all to conduct their deeds with great alacrity and great love, so that the king knows the goodness of their hearts toward him and elevates and exalts them. How much more should we be zealous in the service of our King and Creator, to find favor before Him, that He atone for our sins and that our Torah study be pleasing before Him, that we be called His servants — for it is explained in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar 13a) that the psalm, "Behold, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord" (Psalms 134:1), refers to those who stand to occupy themselves with Torah from midnight onward. And certainly one should be called "a servant of the Lord" only if he is complete in every kind of service, and if the service is directed exclusively to Him, blessed be He, without any ulterior motive — for if there is any ulterior motive for that service, that motive becomes the cause of the service, and once the cause is nullified, the service is nullified, and this is not called "serving the Lord."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:54: In this same manner, if a person rises early to read Torah at midnight in order to attain one of the levels that Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote of in his book — to attain wisdom, or to have his livelihood arranged for him, as is explained in Parashat Emor (90a) on the verse, "He has given food to those who fear Him" (Psalms 111:5), said regarding those who occupy themselves with Torah from midnight onward, and the many other virtues written in the Zohar — then these motives become the cause of his Torah reading, and he is comparable to one who reads [Torah] in order that he be called "Rav" or that he be called "Rabbi."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:55: Rashbi, peace be upon him, needed to write all these virtues, in the manner that our holy Torah needed to write the reward for the commandments in this world, in Parashat "If you walk in My statutes" (Leviticus 26:4), "and I will give your rains in their season..." — so that from [performance] not for its own sake, one comes to [perform] for its own sake.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:56: It may also be said that the intent of our holy Torah in mentioning the reward for the commandments is to say that when we perform the commandments for the sake of Heaven, and unify His supernal attributes properly, this reward will necessarily follow in any case, both in this world and in the World to Come — for according to how the soul arouses the flow from above, it is necessarily given its portion from what it has rectified. So too the matter with one who occupies himself with Torah from midnight onward — he attains all those virtues from what he has done, and they are not external virtues unrelated to the deed, God forbid, but rather all those virtues are related to the deed and flow from it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:57: Therefore the intelligent person should take to heart to perform his service for the sake of Heaven without any ulterior motive, for He who examines hearts and minds knows whether his service is pleasing before Him and clean, or not. For when the Holy One, blessed be He, sees, with His supernal providential eye, that a person's service is not proper before Him, He places a stumbling block before him, so that the virtues that Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote of do not materialize for him — to push him away from being called one of the servants of the Lord — and thereby tests whether his service is constant before Him or not, and by this one is distinguished between one who serves God and one who does not serve Him: if he serves in order to receive a reward, when the reward is nullified his service is nullified; but one who serves in order not to receive a reward, his service is always constant and is never nullified by any cause — and he is called "a servant of the Lord" and not "a servant of the reward." So too should one be called one who occupies himself with Torah "for its own sake," as explained — that he occupies himself with it only to do the will of his Maker.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:58: In this, Rabbi Yosei, peace be upon him, instructs in the passage before us, which we quoted from Parashat Vayikra, saying that that flame comes from above, from the side of Gevurah, and from the side of the angel Gabriel, who is the supernal herald that gives forth six voices, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Parashat Shelach Lecha, end, 171b), striking the wings of the rooster, and it trembles and gazes and considers, because of the honor of its Master, to do His will, and calls out to the people — therefore it is called "sechvi" (gazing) — explaining that just as the supernal herald calls the supernal souls to stand for the service of the Creator, occupying themselves with Torah — for until midnight each one occupies himself with Torah and reflects on what he did during the day — so the lower herald calls to lower human beings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:59: And so they explain there (same page) that after midnight the flame of the pillar of Isaac goes forth and strikes this rooster, who is called "gever," in the manner of the other, supernal "gever" [angel] over it. Once this "gever" strikes it, it crows and gives six calls, all with wisdom. At the hour it crows, all the roosters of this world crow, and another flame goes forth from it and reaches them beneath their wings, and they crow — what does it crow? At the first hour it crows and says, "the voice of the Lord is with power, the voice of the Lord is with majesty" (Psalms 29:4); at the second hour it crows and says, "the Lord's voice cries to the city" (Micah 6:9); at the third hour it crows and says, "the voice of the Lord hews out flames of fire" (Psalms 29:7); at the fourth hour it crows and says, "the voice of the Lord makes the wilderness to tremble" (Psalms 29:8); at the fifth hour it crows and says, "the voice of the Lord is upon the waters..." (Psalms 29:3); at the sixth hour it crows and says, "the voice of the Lord makes the hinds to calve..." (Psalms 29:9); afterward it crows and says, "a voice says, Cry! And I said, What shall I cry?..." (Isaiah 40:6), and this is the rooster that crows and does not cease, and afterward it crows as before — and what does it crow? All the deeds of the people of the world, because it is the master of the [heavenly] pen and the scribe's inkwell at its loins, and it writes down all the deeds of the people of the world every day, and at night, after it has finished all its callings, it crows all that was written during the day — so far his words, as pertains to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:60: Here it is explicit that the supernal herald calls him "rebuked" — and this herald is called Gabriel, as is explained at the end of its words, that the scribe's inkwell is at its loins, and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat 55a) that this refers to Gabriel. And it says, at the hour it crows, all the roosters of this world crow; and so it is likewise explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach 172b), which speaks there of midnight, [saying]: the herald stands firm, calls out with power and proclaims, and then how many are those who prepare a song and perform the service! And it further says there, and they sing until morning ascends. And so in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, end, 21) it explains that at the beginning of the night all the gates are locked and all the holy ones sit silently, and the external forces spread through the world, and it says, when the night is divided, the herald stands and proclaims, and the gates are opened, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:61: Now, when the intelligent person considers and takes these matters to heart, it is fitting that he be aroused in his spirit and be zealous to give honor to his Creator upon hearing the crowing of the rooster, which is the lower herald drawn from the supernal herald — just as those above are aroused upon hearing the voice of the supernal herald to give honor to their Creator. And he should consider in his mind: were he in the King's palace and heard the voice of the king's herald calling upon his servants to stand for the king's service, how zealously he would rise, fearing lest they punish him! Why then should he not fear upon hearing the voice of the rooster, since those who know the hidden things have explained to us that it crows by the power of the supernal herald, and he should fear lest the ledgers of his debts be called out before it and he be punished. For it says that after six hours, which is the time of the rising of the dawn, then it calls out all the deeds it wrote during the day; and if a person is then occupied with Torah, Torah is sufficient to erase his transgressions, so that he may repent. Further, one who rises at night to occupy himself with Torah — the Torah makes known to him his sin so that he may repent, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra 23b) on the verse, "or his sin, which he has committed, be made known to him" (Leviticus 4:23). But if he is asleep at that time, what will he answer for his sins? Certainly he deserves punishment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:62: And so Rabbi Elazar, peace be upon him, explains in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Metzora), in these words: Rabbi Elazar opened, "and like birds caught in a snare, so are the sons of men snared" (Ecclesiastes 9:12) — this verse has already been explained, but come and see, people do not know, do not hear, and do not consider the will of their Master, and a herald calls out concerning them every day, and there is none who listens to it. At the hour night falls and the gates are shut, the female aspect of the great abyss is aroused, and how many bands of destroyers are found in the world! Then the Holy One, blessed be He, casts sleep upon all the people of the world, even upon all in whom there is an arousal of life, and they roam the world and inform people of matters, some false and some true, while people are bound in sleep. When the north wind is aroused and the night is divided, the herald goes forth, and the Holy One, blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous, and then His flames go forth and strike beneath the wings of the rooster and it crows, and all the people of the world stir in their beds, but there is none who arouses his spirit for the service. When morning comes, the herald calls out, and all the supernal hosts and camps praise the Holy One, blessed be He — this is what is written, "when the morning stars sang together" (Job 38:7) — then how many gates open on every side, and the gate of Abraham opens through the Community of Israel, to invite all the people of the world — this is what is written, "and he planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba" (Genesis 21:33) — yet there is none who arouses his spirit for the service of his Master. With what face shall he stand before the King when they arouse judgment against him and seize him with a collar, and no merit is found for him to be saved? Then it is written, "and like birds caught in a snare, so are the sons of men snared" — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:63: This shows that a person is called to judgment if he awakens from his sleep at midnight and does not rise to read Torah, and the great punishment is [greater still] when daylight comes and he does not rise to praise his Creator in the morning prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:64: And so in Chupat Eliyahu it says, in these words: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says, over three things the Holy One, blessed be He, weeps: over a Torah scholar who has no bread in his basket; over a Torah scholar who does not occupy himself with Torah during the last watch [of the night], concerning whom the verse says, "As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed" (Proverbs 26:14); and over one who is arrogant for no reason — so far his words. The matter of this weeping over a Torah scholar who does not occupy himself with Torah during the last watch is because the essential purpose of Torah in a scholar is to give honor to the One who gave him the Torah, and if he does not give honor to the Torah, the Torah is found to be, in him, almost in vain. Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, complains against him, having given him the Torah, which is His daughter, and yet he does not treat her properly, as will be further explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:65: And so it is proven in several places in the Zohar that the essential purpose of rising early to read Torah is to bind night to day. And so it appears in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit 4a), that a certain voice is aroused in the Garden of Eden and says: which of you awaits, every day, the light that shines at the hour the King commands the doe [i.e., dawn], and the King is honored above all the kings of the world? Whoever does not anticipate this every day in that world has no portion here — so far his words. My teacher, peace be upon him, explained that the reality of this illumination that shines "at the hour the King commands the doe" is at the time of the rising of the dawn, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach 46a), in these words: and when morning comes, the Community of Israel comes and delights with the Holy One, blessed be He, and He extends to her the scepter of Chesed, and it does not rise alone but rises together with those who join with her; and this has already been stated, as it is written, "By day the Lord commands His kindness, and in the night..." (Psalms 42:9).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:66: And there, at the end of the column, are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in these words: when night is removed and morning comes and it grows dark and dim [again, at day's end], then the King and the Matronita are in the mystery of joy, and He gives her gifts, and to all the members of His palace; fortunate is the portion of whoever is counted among them — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:67: And so it is further explained there (beginning of Parashat Pinchas), in these words: Rabbi Shimon said, as it were, all those who merit to occupy themselves with Torah from when the night is divided, and come to the Matronita — when day dawns, to receive the face of the King, he is strengthened and takes possession within the Shechinah, and not only that, but Chesed rests upon him, as we have established — so far his words. And so it is likewise explained there (Parashat Miketz 194b), the verse, "The Lord favors those who fear Him, those who wait for His kindness" (Psalms 147:11), regarding those who rise at midnight and wait until day to receive the thread of Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:68: These passages make clear the obligation incumbent on one who occupies himself with Torah from midnight onward, to bind night to day; and so it is further explained there (Zohar Parashat Vayikra, end of 25a), in these words: and when the holy doe is aroused by the north wind and descends, that fortunate one who possesses her arises and strengthens himself like a mighty lion in Torah until morning comes, and goes with that holy doe to appear before the King, to receive one thread of Chesed — so far his words. This is even more clearly explained. And it says, "that fortunate one who possesses her arises" — my teacher, peace be upon him, explained a great matter in these words: that the rising at midnight must be to bind oneself to the Shechinah, like a man who is zealously protective of his wife and does not want her love to be separated from him, and there is pleasure only from the side of love. So the righteous person is zealously protective, not wanting the Shechinah to be separated from him, to abandon him, and for her love to be separated from him; and therefore, out of the greatness of his love for her, he rises to do her will, to occupy himself with Torah, for through occupation with Torah he unites with her — and certainly, whoever rises to occupy himself with Torah out of this yearning of love mentioned will not fall asleep. To this Rashbi, peace be upon him, refers in saying, "and strengthens himself like a mighty lion until morning comes."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:69: One who rises at midnight is a model of the supernal Righteous One for the mystery of union, and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Emor 90a) on the verse, "He has given food (teref) to those who fear Him" (Psalms 111:5), in these words: what is "He has given food to those who fear Him"? Rather, it is written, "and rises while it is yet night, and gives food to her household" (Proverbs 31:15) — from here we learn that whoever studies Torah at night and rises at midnight, at the hour the Community of Israel is aroused to prepare her house for the King, joins with her, and is called "master of the King," and they give him, every day, from those preparations of the house — this is what is written, "and gives food to her household and a portion (chok) to her maidens" — who is her household? All who join with her at night are called "her household," "members of her household." And therefore "He has given food to those who fear Him" — what is "food" (teref)? Literal food, which is taken from a distant, supernal place, as it is written, "she brings her food from afar" (Proverbs 31:14); and who merits this food? The end of the verse proves it, as it is written, "He shall remember His covenant forever" (Psalms 111:5) — whoever occupies himself with Torah to join with her at night; and not only that, but the Holy One, blessed be He, has for Himself one supernal Righteous One, and he joins with Him, and both of them inherit [along] with the Community of Israel, "and the righteous shall inherit the land" (Isaiah 60:21) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:70: The reason those who rise at midnight merit the mystery of the "food" mentioned in the passage is because it is measure for measure — just as they cause blessings to be drawn from the holy place, as it is written, "Lift up your hands to the sanctuary" (Psalms 134:2), as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra 13a), so it is fitting that their sustenance be given to them from there — and from the positive statement you may infer the negative. This makes clear the great virtue of one who occupies himself with Torah from midnight onward and binds night to day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:71: And so it is further explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah 130b) that there is praise for the morning prayer when a person joins to it the Torah he studied at night. It says there that when the time of morning arrives, then the herald proceeds and calls out, "Prepare, holy supernal ones who praise your Master"; they are arranged with the praises of the day, and then day is separated from night. Fortunate is the portion of one who rises from the praises of the Torah he studied at night, precisely at that time, for the morning prayer — so far his words. And so its greatness is also explained at the beginning of Parashat Va'etchanan (260a) — see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:72: Just as the reward is great, so the punishment is great for one who does not rise, in the manner explained; and this matter is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, end of 21), in these words: when the night is divided, the herald stands and proclaims, and the gates open; then a certain spirit from the north side is aroused and strikes David's harp, and it plays of itself, and praises the King, and the Holy One, blessed be He, delights with the righteous in the Garden of Eden. Fortunate is the portion of whoever is aroused at that time and occupies himself with Torah; and whoever stands at that time is called a companion of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel, and not only that, but these are called "brothers and friends" to Him, as it is written, "For the sake of my brothers and friends, I will now say, Peace be within you" (Psalms 122:8), and are called "companions," as it is written, "companions listen for your voice" (Song of Songs 8:13). When day comes, the herald stands and proclaims, and the gates of the south side open, and stars and constellations are aroused, and the gates of mercy open, and the King sits and receives praises; then the Community of Israel and all those companions take hold of her wings, and their words come and rest in the King's bosom; then the King commands, and in the book they write all those members of His palace, and a thread of Chesed is drawn upon them, for from that thread a person is crowned with the King's crown, and from it those above and below fear him; and even at the time their Master of Judgment stands to judge the world, he enters through all the King's gates and there is none to prevent him with their hand, and those Masters of Judgment do not judge him. Fortunate is the portion of the righteous who occupy themselves with Torah, and all the more so at the time the King desires words of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:73: Come and see the mystery of the matter: the Community of Israel stands before the King only through the Torah, for as long as Israel is in the Land and occupies itself with Torah, the Community of Israel rests with them; when they cease from the words of Torah, she cannot remain with them a single hour. Therefore, at the hour the Community of Israel is aroused toward the King, her host is strengthened, and the holy kings look to receive them; but whenever the Community of Israel comes to the King and Torah is not found with her, as it were her strength weakens. Woe to those who weaken her strength above! Therefore fortunate are those who occupy themselves with Torah, and all the more so at that hour when the Community of Israel needs it; then the Holy One, blessed be He, calls concerning him, "And He said to me, You are My servant, Israel, in whom I take glory" (Isaiah 49:3) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:74: This passage makes clear our obligation to occupy ourselves with Torah from midnight onward, for by this we give strength to the Shechinah through the arousal of Torah, at a time when the Holy One, blessed be He, longs for words of Torah, and the Shechinah says, "companions listen for your voice, let me hear it," as is explained at the beginning of Parashat Pinchas. And whoever does not rise and does not take care to give arousal-strength to the Shechinah weakens, God forbid, the supernal power, as it says, "as it were her strength weakens; woe to those who weaken the strength above."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:75: Similar to this, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach 172b) on the verse, "If you faint in the day of adversity, your strength is small (tzar koach)" (Proverbs 24:10), regarding one who lets his hands go slack from occupying himself with Torah, in these words: what is "if you faint"? Whoever lets his hands go slack from [attachment to] the Holy One, blessed be He, not strengthening himself in Him — and how does a person strengthen himself in the Holy One, blessed be He? Whoever strengthens himself in Torah — for whoever strengthens himself in Torah strengthens himself in the Tree of Life, and as it were gives strength to the Community of Israel to be strengthened. And if he lets go of the Torah, what is written? "If you faint" — if he lets go of the Torah, "in the day of adversity your strength is small" — on the day trouble comes to him, as it were, he oppresses the Shechinah, who is the strength of the world. And it explains this as "tzar koach Kaf-Heh" [a play reading "your strength" as containing the letters of the Divine Name] — and so it explains further on there. The reason is that since Samael comes to accuse him, and the Shechinah has no defending face with which to answer on his behalf, she stands in constraint and distress, and her power is constricted, and she does not give her strength properly to the lower ones, the children of Israel.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:76: It further explains there, another interpretation of "your strength is small": come and see, at the hour a person lets go of the Torah and walks in an improper path, how many enemies are ready to become his accusers on the day of trouble, and even the person's own soul, which is his strength and power, becomes an owner of a grudge against him, as it is written, "tzar koach" — because it is an adversary (tzar) to him — so far his words. This explains "your strength is small" to mean that his soul, which is his strength, is an adversary and enemy to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:77: It seems to me that certainly whoever rises at midnight with his intent and yearning to give strength to the Shechinah out of love for her — in the manner of "you who make mention of the Lord, take no rest" (Isaiah 62:6), as explained in Parashat Vaera (30a) — a power will be bestowed upon his soul to be able to fast, for they said in the Zohar, which we quoted above, that they make him into a new creature, and certainly a power will be renewed in his soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:78: I have seen how many penitents rise at midnight and occupy themselves with Torah until day and fast, and all of this is divine assistance upon them, "for man does not live by bread alone." And if not, just as he weakens the supernal power, the power of his soul weakens too — these matters are clear, and we have elaborated on this in the Gate of Repentance, chapter 6.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:79: The reason for this is that the night is given for the occupation with Torah, as they said (Shemot Rabbah 47:5, Vayikra Rabbah 19:1, Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:10), "there is no 'song of Torah' except at night" — the intent being from midnight onward, for that is when it is called "night"; before midnight it is called "leil," as is explained in the Tikkunim. In these words, there in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach 46a): Rabbi Yosei opened, "For the leader, upon Ayelet HaShachar (the hind of the dawn), a psalm of David" — how beloved is the Torah before the Holy One, blessed be He! Whoever occupies himself with Torah is beloved above, beloved below; the Holy One, blessed be He, listens to his words, does not forsake him in this world and does not forsake him in the World to Come. And one needs to study Torah by day and by night — why? So that he be found attached to the complete holy Name — for just as there is no day without night, and it is not complete except one with the other, so too regarding Torah, one must be found with it day and night, for it to be a completeness for a person, day and night. And it has already been stated that the essence of night is from midnight onward, and even though the first half is generally included in "night," nevertheless, at midnight the Holy One, blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous, and then a person must rise and occupy himself with Torah — and it has already been stated that the Holy One, blessed be He, and all the righteous listen to him — so far his words, as pertains to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:80: And in the Tikkunim (2) it says that from midnight onward it is called "night," in these words: masters of Torah, from the side of the middle pillar, in which, at midnight, David used to rise to join himself with the Shechinah, who is called "night," and he is "the watchman, what of the night" (Isaiah 21:11), "a night of watching (leil shimurim) it is for the Lord" (Exodus 12:42) — a guarded night for YHVH; and concerning this it is said, whoever occupies himself with Torah at night, the Holy One, blessed be He, draws upon him a thread of Chesed by day, as it is said, "By day the Lord commands His kindness, and in the night His song is with me" (Psalms 42:9) — so far his words. This clearly explains our intent. And so what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, "whoever occupies himself with Torah at night, the Holy One, blessed be He, draws upon him...," and so on, the intent is regarding the aspect called "night," which is from midnight onward, as is likewise explained in the passage we quoted above from Parashat Vayikra (end of 21).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:81: From this passage that we quoted from the Tikkunim, it appears explicitly that only those who occupy themselves with Torah from midnight onward are called "masters of Torah," corresponding to the attribute of Jacob — as it says, "from the side of the middle pillar, in which, at midnight, David used to rise to join himself with his Shechinah." The reason Rashbi needed to say this matter is to explain the term "masters of Torah," whose wording in the Holy Tongue is "ba'al Torah" (possessor/master of Torah). Now, regarding "chasidim" (pious ones) and "gibborim" (mighty ones), corresponding to Chesed and Gevurah, he already explained the reason above; but the reason for those who occupy themselves with Torah to be called "masters of Torah" and not "those who occupy themselves with Torah" — he answers, because they unify the attribute of Torah with night, as David used to do, rising at midnight to join himself with his Shechinah through occupation with Torah — and especially in light of what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha 92b) regarding "at midnight I will rise to give thanks to You" (Psalms 119:62), the matter is well resolved.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:82: This is the matter of occupying oneself with Torah "for its own sake," which is explained in the Tikkunim (2a), that the intent is to unify the Holy One, blessed be He, the Name YHVH, with the Shechinah — and this is [the meaning of] "for its own sake" (lishmah), for the sake of the Name (leshem Hashem).
